..
A dryer pattern begins to move into the Marianas as the last of the
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms associated with Jangmi
have shifted west of the region. The Marianas will be mostly dry
tonight before a weak trade wind trough moves through, bumping up
shower coverage from isolated to scattered Saturday. Moisture will
remain high enough to retain at least isolated showers for the rest
of the forecast period. The potential for lighter winds by mid next 
week may allow for some island effect showers to develop but this
remains uncertain.

Marine...
Surf observations show that the southwest swell generated by the
westerly wind burst associated with Jangmi peaked last night but was
smaller than previously forecasted. Therefore combined seas are now 
4 to 6 feet and dropping gradually through the weekend. An additional
pulse of west swell may briefly push seas and surf back up around 
Monday depending on the strength of Jangmi. There is a moderate risk 
of rip currents tonight for east, south, and west facing reefs and a 
low risk for north facing reefs. South facing reefs may drop to low 
risk by tomorrow night. Light to moderate southeasterly winds are 
expected to turn easterly by late tomorrow.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Jangmi (06W) continues to move northwest into the
Philippine Sea and away from Micronesia. Jangmi is located near  
16N133E with maximum sustained winds around 45 mph as of the 1PM ChST
update from JTWC. Widespread showers wrap around the southern side 
of the center, while relatively drier air in the mid- levels is 
causing showers to be more scattered to low-end numerous in coverage
north of the center, but this has started to improve over the pass
few hours. South of TS Jangmi, scatterometer data shows moderate to 
fresh monsoon southwesterly winds extend across Palau and western Yap
State, producing scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. TS 
Jangmi will continue to move northwest and away from Micronesia, and
is forecast to intensify over the next couple of days, possibly 
becoming a typhoon Saturday night. This will keep Palau and Yap in 
the monsoonal flow over at least the next couple though this pattern 
is expected to slowly weaken as Jangmi and the monsoon trough move
further away from the region.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery and scatterometer analysis show a surface trough 
extending from a buffer circulation near the Equator and 150E to 
between Chuuk and Pohnpei. A second surface trough extends from 
east-southeast of Kosrae and through an elongated circulation south 
of Majuro near 4N171E and then merges with the Inter-Tropical 
Convergence Zone (ITCZ) east of Majuro. These feature are generating 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms across Pohnpei and 
across the southern Marshall islands, just south and east of Majuro. 
Kosrae is currently in between these features and besides for some 
island-effect showers due to light winds, showers have been fairly 
spotty near the island and surrounding coastal waters.

Forecast models support both troughs shifting westward, with the
trough currently between Chuuk and Pohnpei becoming more west-east 
oriented. These features will support an overall wet pattern across
the region this weekend with periods of scattered showers and 
isolated thunderstorms. As the surface trough south of Majuro shifts
west-northwest, winds will become light to gentle and will start to 
shift southward early next week for Majuro and Kosrae and becoming 
variable at Pohnpei. Looking toward middle and second half on next 
week, model guidance begin to diverge. The deterministic GFS shows 
the surface troughs and the ITCZ weakening and shifting southward, 
which would support relatively drier weather. The deterministic ECMWF
also shows the surface troughs and ITCZ weakening, but the southward
shift is slower which extends the overall wetter pattern into the 
latter half of the week. The ensembles of both the ECMWF and GFS show
this spread but trends do support a slightly drier pattern for the 
second half of the week before potentially increasing next weekend, 
so reflect that trend in the forecast by limiting the potential for
showers to 20 percent at Pohnpei, Kosrae and Majuro.

Altimetry data shows seas are around 3 to 5 feet around Pohnpei and
Kosrae and closer to 5 to 7 feet across the Marshall Islands, driven
mostly by the easterly trade swell and subsiding northerly swell. As
winds become light to gentle across region and become more southerly
at Majuro and Kosrae and variable at Pohnpei early next week, seas
are expected to drop about a foot as wind waves and the easterly
swell subside slightly.
